title: Trunk part masses (thorax, abdomen, pelvis, shoulder girdle) of adult males by CT

quantity.name: segment mass
quantity.definition: mean mass of trunk parts (kg, text) and rounded % body mass of body parts (Fig 10A, combining this study's trunk data with literature data for other segments)

source.sample: 15 male patients (each scanned for one trunk portion only: 5 subjects per portion); male patients of the Institute of Radiology and Radiotherapy, Medical University Gdansk; CT 8-mm layers
source.notes: DOI derived from printed PII S0021-9290(97)00013-4. Subject body mass/height not reported in extracted text.

protocol.summary: CT-based geometric and inertial data of the trunk divided into thorax, abdomen, pelvis and shoulders; tissue composition.
how_to_use: For models that separate the shoulder girdle from the thorax, use thorax 11 %, abdomen 16 %, pelvis 11 % and each shoulder 5 % of body mass (Fig 10A, integers).
Absolute means (thorax 8.1, abdomen 11.4, pelvis 8.0, shoulder girdle 8.0 kg) need the (unreported) body mass to be normalised – use the % values instead.
Treat as low-precision (n=5 per portion, integers in Fig 10A).

measurement.device: CT, 8-mm layers; tissue-specific densities; trunk modelled as non-circular right frusta between anthropometric landmarks

protocol.notes: Real trunk = thorax (TH) + abdomen (AB) + pelvis (PE); shoulder girdle (SG) = right + left shoulder (SH) – shoulders separated from the thorax; viscera-trunk = AB + PE; whole trunk = real trunk + shoulder girdle. Boundaries are anthropometric landmarks (Fig 1); the thorax here EXCLUDES the shoulder girdle, unlike Pearsall/de Leva.

extraction.uncertainty: absolute masses: as printed (0.1 kg); Fig 10A values are printed integer labels (±0.5 % rounding)
extraction.check_notes: Re-read text (Inertial quantities, p.684) and Fig 10A labels at 150 dpi. Fig 10A labels sum to 100 % with hand = 1 % (label partly obscured: 'HA 1'). Text OCR '8.0 ke.' = 8.0 kg. No numeric tables exist in this PDF despite catalog note; COM data are only in Figs 6-8 (not digitised: complex nomograms).

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
